name: Tajik National Park (Mountains of the Pamirs)
blurb: Glaciers, steppe and the wild sheep, snow leopards and vultures of the Pamirs.

tip.title: Shrink the glaciers
tip.text: Glacial meltwater wets the high meadows in a dry land. Set Glacial meltwater to -100% and watch the sedges, then the sheep, ibex and the predators that follow them.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Sedges grow in damp alpine ground; Wikipedia notes sedges are a main food of argali and of ibex in spring and summer.

nodes.name: Marco Polo sheep
nodes.desc: The Pamir argali is the largest argali race. Argali eat grasses, sedges and forbs and are hunted mainly by wolves and snow leopards.
A cliff-dwelling goat of steep, rocky ground above the tree line. It eats alpine grasses and herbs, and twigs in winter.
A large mountain game bird, the most recorded bird near the park, living on high rocky slopes and meadows.

nodes.name: Horned lark
nodes.desc: A small ground bird of open, bare alpine and steppe ground that eats seeds and insects.
A small hunter of burrows and open ground. GloBI records it eating small birds such as horned larks.

nodes.name: Yellow-billed chough
nodes.desc: A flocking mountain crow that forages on the ground for seeds and invertebrates and scavenges around human camps.
A scavenger whose diet is mostly bone and marrow from the carcasses of mid-sized hoofed animals, which it drops to crack open.
An elusive cat that preys on wild sheep and goats such as argali and ibex, and also on marmots and other small mammals.

nodes.name: Grey wolf
nodes.desc: Wikipedia calls Himalayan wolves the main predator of argali, taking animals of any age, especially in deep winter snow.
A large raptor of crags and open slopes. GloBI records it eating marmots and stoats; argali lamb remains have been found in nests.
Strong high-altitude sunlight drives the short summer growing season.
Glaciers such as Fedchenko feed streams and wet meadows in a very dry climate.
Cold, dry, stony soils hold few nutrients and recycle them slowly.

nodes.name: Soil microbes
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil, slowly in the cold.
